items.stem: What is meant by 'balanced institutional design' in the context of the authority of a constitution?
items.answer: The arrangement of institutions so that no single institution can dominate and power is checked.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: balanced institutional design correctly explained as the arrangement of institutions so that no single institution can dominate and power is checked.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the making of the Indian Constitution is NOT correct?
items.answer: The Constituent Assembly took decisions mainly by majority vote without discussion.

options: The composition of the Constituent Assembly followed the plan proposed by the British Cabinet Mission.
The Constituent Assembly took decisions mainly by majority vote without discussion.
The Objectives Resolution of December 1946 set out the aspirations and values behind the Constitution.
The ideals of the national movement, such as equality, liberty and democracy, shaped the Constitution.

items.stem: "A constitution's provisions must be fair." Examine this statement with reference to the authority of a constitution.
items.answer: The statement is valid. People respect and follow a constitution when it protects the interests and rights of all.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (people respect and follow a constitution when it protects the interests and rights of all.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:

items.answer: They wanted institutions suited to Indian conditions and values, not simple copies.

Members need basic rules that allow coordination and assure them that others will also follow the rules.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the need for a constitution and answer the questions that follow.
"The Indian Constitution allows the government to take positive welfare measures, some of which are legally enforceable. A constitution expresses the fundamental identity of a people. A constitution sets limits on the powers of the government through rights that it cannot violate."
(i) Before 1975, the kingdom of Sikkim was ruled by a: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'coordination and assurance' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The Indian Constitution includes directive goals of social justice. (2)
items.answer: (i) monarch called the Chogyal (ii) The first function of a constitution: a set of basic rules that allow minimal coordination and trust among members of society. (iii) It aims to enable the government to fulfil the aspirations of society and create a just society.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) monarch called the Chogyal (ii) The first function of a constitution: a set of basic rules that allow minimal coordination and trust among members of society. (iii) It aims to enable the government to fulfil the aspirations of society and create a just society.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the making of the Indian Constitution is correct?

items.stem: What is meant by 'limitation of power' in the context of the need for a constitution?
items.answer: The function of a constitution that sets limits on what a government can impose on its citizens, for example through fundamental rights.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: India adopted the first past the post system from Britain.

items.stem: The following statement about the making of the Indian Constitution is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The members of the Constituent Assembly were elected directly by all adult citizens."

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Objectives Resolution of December 1946 set out the aspirations and values behind the Constitution. The Constitution was preceded by long public discussion and deliberation in the Assembly. The composition of the Constituent Assembly followed the plan proposed by the British Cabinet Mission. The Constituent Assembly worked through committees, and decisions were usually taken by consensus."
(i) Explain the term 'Drafting Committee', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The Constitution reflected the ideals of the national movement. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The Constitution came into force on 26 November 1949." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The committee of the Constituent Assembly chaired by B.R. Ambedkar that prepared the draft of the Constitution. (ii) The movement had long demanded rights, democracy and equality, as in the Nehru Report of 1928 and the Karachi resolution of 1931. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the need for a constitution is correct?

items.stem: The following statement about the authority of a constitution is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The way a constitution is made has no effect on its authority."
items.answer: Constitutions made by unpopular leaders or the military lack authority.
